chunks: A group of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Sinan, from Al-Hasan ibn Al-Sariy, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Adhan is recited slowly (melodiously), and the Iqamah is recited quickly (flowingly).
ai.seo_question: What is the difference in recitation style between the Adhan and the Iqamah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates the distinct vocal aesthetics of the two calls, prescribing *tarteel* (slow, melodious recitation) for the Adhan to invite contemplation, and *hadr* (rapid, brisk recitation) for the Iqamah to signal urgency. This distinction, preserved in *Al-Kafi*, underscores the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the spiritual atmosphere of the call versus the practical immediacy of commencing prayer. The ruling highlights the Prophet's tradition of adapting vocal delivery to the specific function of each call within the ritual framework.
